To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
1) the nuclear DNA content of liver cirrhosis is diploid; 2) the nuclear DNA contents of liver tumours induced by AAF is diploid.

Flow cytometry of DNA content in liver tumours in acetylaminoflurene-treated rats revealed a diploid DNA-content in well-differentiated hepatocellular carcinomata and in cirrhosis and proliferating oval cells.
the DNA-contents of liver tumours in AAF-fed rats were diploid.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the analysis of the nuclear DNA content of rat liver tumours by means of FCM.
the analysis of the DNA contents of liver tumours and cirrhotic liver nodules in rats exposed to AAF.
the analysis of nuclear DNA content and cell proliferation in rat livers exposed to acetyl-aminofluoreine.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
in this model system, liver cirrhosis is not accompanied by a change of the nuclear DNA content of the liver cells.
the liver tumours induced in rats exposed to AAF were not aneuploid, but diploid and derived from the hepatocytes.
the diploid stem-lines in these liver tumours are derived from the diploid stem-line of the cirrhotic liver tissue.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the nuclear DNA contents of the liver tumours in the two experiments were diploid.

the nuclear DNA-content of liver tumours in AAF-treated rats does not differ from the nuclear DNA-content in cirrhotic liver tissue and that the nuclear DNA-contents in liver tumours in this model are diploid.

in this model of hepatocarcinogenesis, cirrhosis or oval cells proliferation is not a prerequisite for the development of well differentiated hepatocarcinomas, but that these tumours do not arise from diploid stem cells, but rather from aneuploid cells with a high DNA index (1.6-2.2).
The main takeaway from our work is that
flow cytometric analysis of nuclear DNA-content in the rat liver can be used for detection of early changes in the liver.
the liver tumors that we have analyzed are diploid, which is a feature of well differentiated tumors.

flow cytometry is a useful technique to study the nuclear DNA content in rat liver tumours and regenerating nodules, and that it is a sensitive method for detecting diploid stem lines in tumours with aneuploid stem lines.
